study_type.claude: Mixed methods (controlled human study / experiment with mixed methods)
study_type.note: Both describe a controlled study with logs, survey and qualitative coding; the paper calls it a mixed-methods design.

research_method.claude: Controlled human study, 3 ACATs x 3 task types; IDE logs (ccdc-plugin), screen recordings, post-task Likert survey, personalized interviews; descriptive statistics plus open coding with negotiated agreement; 1,909 min of recordings, 1,257 behaviour instances
research_method.nlm: Controlled experiment / mixed methods; quantitative interaction logs and survey, qualitative coding of screen recordings (1,909 min); 3 ACATs x 3 task types
research_method.value: Controlled human study with mixed methods; 3 ACATs (GitHub Copilot, Tabnine, CodeGeeX) x 3 Python task types (ADS, MSD, RTD); VSCode extension logs (ccdc-plugin), screen recordings (1,909 min), post-task Likert survey (with vs. without ACAT) and personalized interviews; descriptive statistics and open coding of interaction behaviours
research_method.note: Counts of behaviour instances (1,257 of 47 behaviours) reported only by Claude (not contradicted).

context.claude: Academic; CS students at Beihang University (China), Python tasks representative of SE education; 27 students
context.nlm: Academic; Beihang University, CS education; 27 CS students
context.value: academic; Beihang University (China), CS students on Python programming tasks; 27 students (10 senior undergraduates, 17 graduate students)

space_applied.note: SPACE operationalizes self-perceived productivity (Efficiency and flow, Performance, Satisfaction and well-being).

ai_discussed.note: AI coding assistants (Copilot, Tabnine, CodeGeeX) are the object of study.

remote_covid.note: Both list work mode 'Remote' only because the experiment was run remotely on the platform; remote work is not a topic of the study.

data_window.note: NotebookLM says 'early 2024'; full text states the survey was conducted in January 2024.

cat_productivity.note: Only self-perceived productivity (survey); task completion rate and duration deliberately not measured. NotebookLM labels acceptance rate 'Productivity / Activity', but it is a suggestion-interaction count.

cat_quality.note: Code-quality evaluation criteria for suggestions (correct syntax, similarity to correct code, readability, style, comments) rated by participants.

cat_satisfaction.note: SPACE Satisfaction and well-being via perceived strenuousness of programming without the tool.

cat_activity.note: Interaction frequency and acceptance counts logged by the IDE extension.

cat_devex.note: 'Efficiency and flow' is the SPACE dimension; DevEx framework not used.

evidence.quote: Our study employs a mixed-methods approach, encompassing both quantitative and qualitative data types.
To achieve this goal, we design a controlled human study involving 27 CS students, simulating real-world programming scenarios.
our 27 participants consist of 6 females and 21 males, with 10 being senior undergraduate students and the remaining 17 graduate students.
To ensure construct validity, we base our measurement on the SPACE framework [17], which defines productivity across five dimensions
we conducted a study with 27 CS students, examining their interactions with 3 widely used ACATs across 5 key dimensions
Given the survey was conducted in January 2024, respondents' feedback reflects their ACAT interactions at that time point.

codequality-related metrics, which assess the technical soundness and clarity of generated code (e.g., correct syntax, similarity to correct code, readability, consistent code style, inclusion of comments)
Satisfaction and well-being: measured through participants' sentiment on reliance, operationalized via the perceived strenuousness of programming without the tool.
Using our extension "ccdc-plugin," we quantify the level of interaction by counting the total number of ACAT recommendations and the number of recommendations accepted by participants.

The quantitative data includes code interaction metrics (e.g., code recommendation acceptance counts) and survey responses (Likert-scale ratings), which provide measurable insights into user engagement and satisfaction.
